claims.text: An empty per-field array denotes no recorded multikey component for that indexed path. Empty arrays also appear in non-multikey index scans: SolarWinds shows {y: []} with isMultiKey: false, and Percona shows {cuisine: []} with isMultiKey: false. (high confidence)

Internally, a nonempty MultikeyPaths vector has one component set per index key-pattern field. Its sets contain zero-based positions in dotted paths. For {"a.b": 1, "a.c": 1}, array prefixes a and a.b produce {{0,1},{0}}. (medium confidence)

Path metadata can allow intersecting range bounds on a scalar field even when another indexed field is an array. For {a:1,b:1} and {a:5,b:[1,2,3]}, the query {a:{$gte:0,$lt:10}} can use [0,10) on a. (high confidence)

Tracking array prefixes does not make arbitrary bounds intersections safe. When two predicates share an array-producing prefix, the planner must account for their $elemMatch context; metadata alone does not establish that predicates match the same array element. (low confidence)

multiKeyPaths maps each indexed field to the prefixes that cause multikey indexing. For an index on a.b, an entry ["a"] identifies the ancestor a as the array-bearing prefix; it does not say that b itself is an array. (high confidence)

Path tracking does not make all predicate combinations safe. Without a shared $elemMatch context, predicates whose paths share an array-bearing prefix cannot generally have their bounds combined safely; an additional array prefix inside the innermost $elemMatch can also block combination. (low confidence)

For an indexed dotted path, the listed string identifies the array prefix rather than necessarily the leaf. Percona demonstrates multiKeyPaths:{"grades.date":["grades"]} for dates inside an array of grade objects; the array boundary is grades. (high confidence)

Internally, MultikeyPaths contains one set of zero-based component positions per indexed field when metadata is available. For {'a.b':1,'a.c':1}, array-producing prefixes a and a.b yield {{0,1},{0}}. An empty outer container represents unavailable path-level tracking; it differs from a populated container whose individual sets are empty. (high confidence)

An empty internal MultikeyPaths vector means the index does not support this tracking; it differs from a correctly sized vector whose component sets are all empty. Do not interpret unavailable path metadata as proof that no indexed path is multikey. (low confidence)

Path-level multikey tracking records which prefixes of each indexed field make an index multikey. In explain, multiKeyPaths maps indexed field names to arrays of those prefixes; isMultiKey alone describes the index as a whole. (high confidence)

For index {a:1,b:1} over {a:5,b:[1,2,3]}, explain can report isMultiKey:true with multiKeyPaths:{a:[],b:["b"]}. The empty a entry means no tracked array-producing prefix for that indexed path, although another indexed field makes the index multikey. (high confidence)

Empty per-field entries also occur for non-multikey indexes. SolarWinds' original explain example has isMultiKey:false and multiKeyPaths:{y:[]}; Percona shows the same combination for borough. Interpret each entry together with isMultiKey and the index key pattern. (high confidence)

Do not treat an empty multikey entry as a general schema guarantee. SERVER-127304 documents index path "e.0" over e:["elem1"]: positional access extracts e[0] without marking e multikey, even though e is an array. (low confidence)

isMultiKey describes the entire index. It can be true while an individual multiKeyPaths entry is empty: Percona shows {cuisine: [], "grades.score": ["grades"]} for a compound index with isMultiKey: true. (high confidence)

multiKeyPaths is structural metadata, not a performance verdict. Read indexBounds and FETCH stages alongside it: Percona shows a multikey compound index with array-prefix metadata and a FETCH, while SolarWinds illustrates an empty per-field array in an IXSCAN beneath FETCH. (high confidence)
